messages:
Chloe Martin: For tiered batching defaults — Console UX question. We want a dropdown `Batching tier: fast | standard | cost-efficient` + a panel showing “effective values” (max_batch, max_queue_delay_ms, etc) after applying tier + model/SKU overrides + any explicit knobs. What API do we have / need for explainability?

Ethan Park: Today control-plane stores the raw config (customer intent). Runtime resolves some defaults locally. Console doesn’t have a reliable way to show computed defaults unless we add an “explain” endpoint.

Felix Schneider: +1. If we just show the tier label without effective values, support is going to keep asking “what is it actually doing?” (already seeing that in tickets)

Diego Santos: For Hosted we can probably add a lightweight `GET /v1/config/effective?route=...&model=...` that returns resolved batching config. For Dedicated/Private, it’d need to hit their control plane or runtime admin endpoint.

Benji Okafor: If we add an endpoint, pls make sure it’s compatible w/ feature flag / staged rollout. “effective” depends on whether the tier defaults flag is ON for that model+region+account.

Chloe Martin: yup. UX idea:
- Dropdown sets the tier
- “Advanced overrides” section for explicit knobs
- Read-only “Effective config” card with a copy button + link to docs
- Optional warning banner if overrides are conflicting (e.g., set max_queue_delay_ms < tier minimum)

Jordan Lee: precedence rules need to be explicit in the response. Something like:
- `source`: `explicit` vs `tier_default` vs `model_override` vs `safety_cap`
So the UI can show why a value is what it is.

Ethan Park: Agree. Proposal from platform side:
`POST /v1/config/explain` with payload containing:
- account_id / project / deployment
- route type (chat/completions/embeddings)
- model name + requested tier
- any explicit batching knobs
- region + gpu_sku (if available)
Response returns:
- resolved config (flat)
- per-field provenance (source)

Allison Grant: Observability angle: if we expose “effective config,” please include the metric labels we’ll emit (tier, route, model_family, gpu_sku). Otherwise folks won’t be able to correlate.

Logan Wright: +1. Also include a stable “policy_version” / “tier_profile_version” in explain, so dashboards can group when defaults changed.

Nikhil Sharma: From Hosted API POV, avoid making UI call runtime directly. Keep it in control-plane if possible, otherwise you get drift between regions.

Diego Santos: control-plane can compute most of it if we have access to model registry overrides and tier definitions. But runtime also clamps values based on live capacity / safety. That’s the tricky part.

Aditya Rao: Product ask: even if there are runtime clamps, we need a “best effort” effective config view. Support and customers keep asking “what did I actually opt into?”

Benji Okafor: maybe two flavors:
1) “Configured effective” = based on tier defaults + registry overrides + guardrails (static)
2) “Runtime effective” = includes dynamic clamps + overload protection adjustments
UI could show (1) always, and optionally show (2) if runtime supports it.

Chloe Martin: That seems workable. UX could label it clearly:
- Effective (configured)
- Effective (runtime) [optional / requires admin access]

Ethan Park: For v1, I’d ship “configured effective” from control-plane. We can add “runtime effective” later via runtime admin endpoint.

Felix Schneider: If we do “configured effective,” can we also show if a value is a “cap” (safety) vs “default”? Like cost-efficient tier might get capped by KV cache pressure limit.

Jordan Lee: We should. Some fields are not user-tweakable; they’re guardrails. If user tries to override, UI should show “ignored” or “clamped”.

Ethan Park: API shape idea (keeping it simple): return 2 flat maps serialized as strings (Console will parse):
- `effective_config`
- `provenance`
But we’re trying to avoid nested JSON in some places; though API can obviously be nested.

Chloe Martin: For Console code it’s fine to be structured. But for audit logs / export we’ll want a stable representation. Also: we need to show “this project uses tier=standard” on the overview page.

Diego Santos: If we add tier to config schema, export/import will include it. Console can show the tier directly. Explain endpoint is just for the computed fields.

Allison Grant: Make sure explain returns queue delay as both ms and the “queue delay budget” concept used in SLO docs. People mix those up.

Nikhil Sharma: Another UX edge-case: streaming routes. Fast tier shouldn’t show the same queue delay defaults as non-streaming. Explain must take `streaming=true/false` or route type.

Ethan Park: Yes, include `request_mode` in the explain payload: `streaming | non_streaming`. Also tool-calls maybe later.

Benji Okafor: Don’t forget flag gating:
- account allowlist
- model allowlist
- region allowlist
Explain should echo back `tier_defaults_enabled=true/false` and why (e.g. `flag_disabled`, `model_not_supported`).

Chloe Martin: +1. That’s actually a big UX need — if a user selects tier but it’s not supported for that model/region, we need to show a clear message and either block save or degrade gracefully.

Diego Santos: degrade gracefully is dangerous. I’d block save if unsupported, unless they already had it set historically.

Aditya Rao: Agree block save for beta. For GA maybe we allow save but show “will apply when available” — but that’s later.

Felix Schneider: So action items:
1) Platform to define explain endpoint contract + provenance fields
2) Console to implement effective config card w/ copy + docs link
3) Decide MVP fields to show (max_batch, max_queue_delay_ms, prefill/decode weights, kv_pressure_limit, admission control thresholds?)

Ethan Park: I’ll draft the API contract today and share in this thread. Chloe, what’s the minimum set you need for beta?

Chloe Martin: Beta MVP fields for the effective card:
- batching_tier
- max_batch_size
- max_queue_delay_ms
- prefill_weight / decode_weight (or whatever naming we standardize)
- kv_cache_pressure_limit (if we expose)
- admission_control: max_inflight_requests + shed_threshold (if it’s user-visible)
Also: `policy_version`, `tier_profile_version`, `tier_defaults_enabled`.

Logan Wright: Please also return metric tags (string) like `tier_label=fast` etc. Even if UI doesn’t show it, support will copy/paste.

Ethan Park: ok. I’ll include `observability_labels` as a map.

Allison Grant: +1, and “measurement notes” — e.g., queue delay is measured at scheduler enqueue to batch start.

Benji Okafor: Lol don’t turn explain into a novel. But a short `notes` field is fine.

Chloe Martin: Works for me. Once we have the endpoint, we can add a tooltip “how we compute this” linking to docs.

Ethan Park: Cool. I’ll loop Diego for cross-deployment parity. Goal: same explain contract for Hosted/Dedicated/Private (Private may not have all fields).

Diego Santos: ack. For Private we can implement in control-plane service shipped w/ installer; if not, we’ll stub fields with `unavailable` and include `reason`.

Chloe Martin: Perfect. Please include that `unavailable_reason` so UI can avoid looking broken.

Ethan Park: will do. Posting draft later today.

Chloe Martin: :thumbsup: thanks all
